newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom in China cellular deal.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom in China cellular deal.

text.p: German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG said on Friday that it would take a 25 percent stake in a cellular phone venture in China that is being set up with Siemens AG, AIG Invest and the China International Trust and Investment Corporation.
"The partners expect around 600,000 subscribers to the network by the year 2010," Telekom said in a statement.

The network will be based on Europe's Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) and will cover the cities Tianjin, Wuhan and Qingdao, which have a combined population of more than 20 million inhabitants.
The deal could give a further boost to the spread of GSM technology, which is the dominant digital cellular communications standard world-wide.

The venture's local partner, the China International Trust and Investment Corporation (CITIC), holds 30 percent of the venture and is also a shareholder in China Unicom, which will operate the GSM networks in the three cities. Siemens will hold 15 percent in the venture, while the German investment bank AIG will hold the remaining 30 percent.

Telekom's mobile communications subsidiary, Deutsche Telekom MobilNet GmbH, said that a so-called roaming agreement, which would allow MobilNet's D1 cellular users to make calls from Chinese GSM networks, would take effect later this year.
